acceptedClaim: For fixed times and strictly positive supplied amplitude-error boxes, monotonic logs and linear OLS weights yield exact box endpoints. Explicit absolute nuisance bounds widen the contrast; absent bounds withhold a physical-alpha interval.
independentMethod: Enumerated every one of 256 original-amplitude box corners on a nonuniform four-time grid, checked 13 malformed-input controls and independently checked the supplied 128 observation realizations against their declared errors.
limitations: This is deterministic interval arithmetic, not a confidence interval or an empirical coverage claim.
The supplied envelope-error guarantee does not follow from a recorded waveform, an AGC setting or a low residual.
A physical-alpha interpretation also assumes a single exponential, shared physical time and stated valid nuisance budgets.
The retained out-of-budget counterexample excludes true alpha; nominal width cannot compensate for a false bound.
The finite engineering ranges in these fixtures do not verify overflow behavior for arbitrary floating-point magnitudes.
nextQuestion: Can a practical one-microphone extraction or independently measured external impulse response invalidate the separated, single-exponential envelope assumptions before applying these conditional bounds?
